title: Rachel Gorman, MSc
text:
I am a research analyst and recent graduate of the M.S. in Applied Digital Sociology program at Hunter College. I am a Research Assistant at the Bridging Divides Initiative, where I study political violence at the national, state, and county levels.
My work combines mixed-methods research, data analysis, open-source investigation, and data visualization. I work primarily with R, Stata, and Tableau, and have experience translating large-scale event and survey data into policy-relevant, partner-facing research products for academic, nonprofit, and industry audiences. My research interests include political violence, far-right digital radicalization, digital gender-based violence, and the relationship between online and offline forms of violence. My academic background in criminology and sociolegal studies has shaped my interest in these areas of study as well as providing a background knowledge on the United States criminal justice system and its underlying power structures.
Research Experience
At Hunter College, my research focused on how digital far-right radicalization can transition to violent extremism offline. I used mixed methods approaches to examine how digital spaces, ideology, gender, and political violence intersect.
My graduate research included examining language use on self-populated far right and white supremacist websites, with a focus on ideological, gendered, and violent language. I also studied the role of the state in political violence by examining police presence, use of force, and the escalation of violence at political protests.
My work has also included working with large-scale datasets and translating complex data into accessible visualizations and research products. My final research project at Hunter College examined leaked data from the white supremacist dating website Whitedate.net and resulted in a publicly available data visualization dashboard.
Independent Research
In addition to my academic and professional research, I am developing and maintaining open-source datasets related to political violence and government activity.
My primary ongoing project tracks ICE and CBP shootings and detention center deaths using publicly available sources. The dataset is compiled, coded, and maintained by me, with plans to expand the dataset historically. Once published, the data will be available for public download.
Academic Background
My academic background is in Criminology and Sociolegal Studies, with a focus on the United States carceral system and underlying power structures.
I received an M.S. in Applied Digital Sociology from Hunter College, a B.A. in Criminology with a minor in Sociolegal Studies from the University of Denver, and an A.A. in Criminal Justice from SUNY Ulster.
At the University of Denver, I worked as a research assistant under Professor Michael Gibson-Light, using qualitative methods for a project on unionizing working prisoners in the United States in the 1970s.
Etc.
Most of my non-academic career time has been spent working in either independent bookstores or bars. I am passionate about small presses and translated fiction, experimenting with variations on a classic Negroni, and mending clothing. I currently reside in New York City where you can find me hanging out at the Rockaways, reading in a park, or exploring the streets looking for cats in dumpsters.

title: Current Projects
text:
OkStupid Data Dashboard
In January 2026, a hacker collective called Martha Root leaked data from the far-right white supremacist dating website whitedate.net, a platform that described itself as a site for “Europids seeking tribal love.”. “Europids” is a term commonly used in white supremacist and eugenicist spaces. The language reflects racist beliefs that race is biologically fixed and hierarchical, a sentiment that is quite common in modern far-right extremist communities. After scrubbing private emails and direct messages, Martha Root publicly released the remaining dataset (here is the link to their project). This project explores this data through a series of visualizations created for a Data Visualization course at Hunter College in May 2026.
The original dataset contained 8,177 user entries. After cleaning, the final working dataset used for analysis contained 8,130 entries. Each visualization was then cleaned and recoded independently.


ICE/CBP Deaths
ICE/CBP Shootings and Detention Center Deaths Dataset {Link to Dataset in Progress, Currently Unavailable}
This is an original dataset compiled from open-source data that tracks deaths and shootings related to ICE and CBP from 2026-2024, with plans to expand through 2012. This dataset is a work in progress which is compiled, coded, and maintained by me. Once published, all information will be available for public download. Please direct any questions/concerns/issues with the dashboard to my email. this is test text.
